comment: The pager's boundaries. Its client: the VMM process that maps a memory region (vmmemory.Mapping), as connection_linux.go speaks to it; the test client is mapping and batchedMapping in vmmemory/memory_test.go, and the campaigns attach with batchedMapping on odd seeds. Its backing: a volume (volume.Volume), which reads object storage, its cache and, for a migration's destination, a peer host; the test backings are backing, slowBacking and peerBacking. Its arena: the Linux arena's memfds (vmmemory/linux.go), which allocate memory as a page is put at a slot; the test arena is arena in memory_test.go. Its spill: a file on a local device (platform.File through zirconvm.SpillStorage), a simulated disk in the campaigns. Any error a guest's request is answered with ends its session, as Connection.serveFaults ends it, and a campaign's host then closes the machine (vmmemory/machine_test.go). An error of the caller's own making (a range outside the file, a context the caller ended) is not listed. See scripts/check-faults.py.

faults.purpose: a command whose answer never came, so the pager cannot tell whether the client applied it: the region is terminal from here; the file is given before the answer is lost
a command whose answer never came, so the pager cannot tell whether the client applied it: the region is terminal from here; the file is not dropped
the client out of VMAs refuses before it touches anything; the fault is served again once a revocation lands
a command whose answer never came, so the pager cannot tell whether the client applied it: the region is terminal from here; the pages are mapped before the answer is lost
as Map's refusal, for zeros
a command whose answer never came, so the pager cannot tell whether the client applied it: the region is terminal from here; the zeros are mapped
a revocation the client out of VMAs refuses, which no fault can serve again: terminal for the region
a command whose answer never came, so the pager cannot tell whether the client applied it: the region is terminal from here; the page stays mapped
a command whose answer never came, so the pager cannot tell whether the client applied it: the region is terminal from here; the access is not completed
a command whose answer never came, so the pager cannot tell whether the client applied it: the region is terminal from here; the pages stay writable
a batch the client out of VMAs refuses before any of its commands lands
a command whose answer never came, so the pager cannot tell whether the client applied it: the region is terminal from here; every run of the batch is mapped
as Revoke's refusal, for a batch
a command whose answer never came, so the pager cannot tell whether the client applied it: the region is terminal from here; no run of the batch is revoked

faults.none: the volume's size, which it holds

faults.purpose: the volume could not read the range: its object store or its cache failed, a sealed source's ReadDirty failed, or its VM ended (ErrNeedsRecovery). The fault fails, and the guest's session with it (TASK-112 would serve a store's refusal once it answers); a prefetch's read that fails ends nothing

faults.error: the VM is not this host's
faults.purpose: ErrHandedOff, ErrClosed or ErrNeedsRecovery: MemoryRegion.Verify fails, and the session ends, as Connection.verify ends it
the segments of the checkpoint index the range falls in could not be read, or the VM ended: the fault that looked the range up fails

faults.none: the volume's page, which it holds
whether the volume is an ephemeral disk, which it holds

faults.purpose: as Load's: the read of a window's wanted pages fails
a migration's peer backing could not reach the source host, or the source could not read its seal: the fault fails

faults.none: the embedded vmmemory.UnpublishedLoader, whose method has an entry of its own
it tells the backing which pages the region holds, and returns nothing

faults.purpose: making a memfd, or mapping it, failed for want of descriptors or memory: an attach fails, a machine that never starts, and a child's fault that needed its fork point's file fails

faults.none: reading a slot of a memfd this process made and maps reads memory, and does not fail; a slot outside the file (ErrRange) is the caller's own

faults.purpose: the slot's page could not be allocated, of the pod's memory (MADV_POPULATE_WRITE) or of the HugeTLB pool (fallocate), before anything was written: the fault or the copy that wanted the page fails

faults.none: punching a slot of a memfd frees its page and does not fail: the kernel's interruption is retried, and a slot outside the file is the caller's own

faults.purpose: as Write's, for a run of slots made zeros: none of the run holds a page

faults.none: it compares two slots through this process's own mapping, and does not fail
an fstat of a memfd this process holds open does not fail
as Release's punch: a file whose kernel cannot say where its data is is walked slot by slot
unmapping and closing a memfd releases it whatever the calls return

faults.purpose: the spill's device failed a fault's read of a spilled page: the page's bytes are not to be had, and the fault fails
the spill's device failed an eviction's write: the victim keeps its slot and its bytes, its mappings already taken away, and the allocation that evicted it fails
the spill file could not be emptied: vmmemory.New fails, a host that never starts, or Close reports it

faults.none: the spill is scratch, never synced
the spill never asks its size
the spill's owner closes the file, not the pager
the embedded platform.File, whose methods have entries of their own

faults.purpose: the spill file's extent could not be reserved: vmmemory.New fails, a host that never starts
the device has no room for the spill's extent: vmmemory.New fails, a host that never starts
